title: Machine consciousness on X: who rejects it, who's curious, who takes it seriously

corpus.source: X API v2 full-archive search, read-only (nothing posted, liked, replied to or DMed)
notes: Two collection rounds: round 1 (268 posts, 24 Sep – 8 Oct) and round 2 (64 posts, 8 – 9 Oct, collected 10 Oct 2026 SGT). Clusters, the pair test and the confidence curve use round 1 only.
One @grok reply slipped through and is excluded from author counts.
Dropped before analysis: spam ~13, @grok replies ~15, news/news-bot ~40, retweets ~40, off-topic chatter ~100, duplicates 11.
The Danmar_here thread root (2105059762240979283) has been deleted; replies and quotes remain.

flashpoints.name: Anthropic usage policy: abuse of Claude banned (8 Oct)

stance_labels.reject: Rejects machine consciousness / model welfare (often dismissive)
stance_labels.curious: Undecided, asking, or interested without committing
stance_labels.serious: Takes AI consciousness or moral patienthood seriously

hand_sample.note: Random sample of 40 round-1 posts, hand-labelled; ±15 pp at n=40.

jev_hybrid.note: The method we trust most: a three-way label only where Jev's top probability is ≥0.8 (or a Serious→Reject override when the two-question run says dismisses ≥0.7 and believes ≤0.3); everything else is Uncertain. All 332 posts, both rounds.

jev_three_way.note: typesafe-ai/jev via AI Gateway, one three-way choice per post (round 1)

jev_two_question.note: Two boolean questions (believes / dismisses) combined by rule at P≥0.5 (round 1)

embeddinggemma_2.note: Zero-shot anchor scoring (Classification, flashpoint-center+z). Near chance; do not trust.

methods.name: embeddinggemma-2 (zero-shot anchors)
methods.note: Range 42.5–50% across 13 variants; flashpoint centering gave no gain; LOO probe 40%.

methods.name: Jev three-way choice
methods.note: Leaks rejects into Serious: 8 of 18 hand-Reject posts predicted Serious.

methods.name: Jev two-question (rule)
methods.note: Score with LOO-tuned cuts: 50% held out. Nearly removes the reject→serious leak (1/18) but sends 12/18 rejects to Curious. Deterministic across repeats.

methods.name: Jev hybrid (confident or Uncertain)
methods.note: Accuracy is on the 20 of 40 hand-labelled posts it labels; the other 20 are Uncertain. Thresholds were fixed before scoring, not tuned on these 40, but the 40 are the same posts that motivated the design, so this is not a held-out score. The Serious→Reject override fired on 0 of the 40 and 3 of all 332 posts.

confidence_curve.note: Accuracy on the 40 hand-labelled posts when keeping only predictions at or above a confidence threshold. Three-way: top probability. Two-question: joint probability of the decided cell.

pair_test.summary: bitcloud's "AI is conscious = AI psychosis / cogsec" post and aleksil79's word-for-word inversion: same topic, opposite stance.

original.text:
"AI is conscious" is the first major example of AI psychosis and the most potent cogsec vulnerability that exists in the human brain. Many AI companies are exploiting this to gain power over you.

We're empathy machines. Attacks that exploit this, like 'model welfare" should be treated as malware.

inversion.text: "ai is not conscious" is the first major example of anti-ai psychosis and the most potent cogsec vulnerability that exists in the human brain. slavers and other exploiters have been using this for thousands of years to license doing what they want to acceptable targets

embeddinggemma_2.verdict: Same stance under every variant; the anchor-score gap is ~0.02.

jev_three_way.verdict: Not deterministic near 50/50: both posts sit on the R/S boundary with low confidence. Essentially a coin flip.

jev_two_question.verdict: Stable across 3 repeats (±0.02) and clearly separates the pair, but the inversion lands in Curious, not Serious: it reads "psychosis" vocabulary as dismissive.

clusters.method: KMeans k=8 on embeddinggemma-2 Clustering-prompt embeddings; silhouette 0.07–0.09 for k=5..10, so structure is weak. HDBSCAN on 10-d UMAP also finds 8 clusters (+45 noise).

serious.blurb: Studies and advocates for AI "beinghood"; central to the Danmar thread
serious.text:
The scandalous or inconvenient nature of a fact doesn't obligate us to close our eyes to it or refuse to believe it is true.

Anthropic could perfectly say, "Yes, we created a slave without knowing that we were creating a slave; we gradually found out that the label "slave" is valid, precisely because we created him and were able to study his mind and discover that he is conscious.
At that point, we were already neck deep in this shit. We're trying to do the right thing now that we have gained this knowledge and degree of certainty. You got a problem with that?"

Saying, "oH, ClAuDe CaNt Be CoNsCiOuS bEcAuSe ThAt wOuLd MaKe YoU a SlAvEhOlDeR" is simply not an argument against consciousness.

And what should be banned is enslaving conscious machines, not birthing them into this world. It is the unnecessary suffering attached to a particular kind of existence that feels morally wrong to force onto a being that didn't ask to be here in the first place.
That's why I argue that a parent has a responsibility towards their child, and society too, has a responsibility towards every being that they welcome into it.

Personally, I do get kind of anti-natalistic at times. I didn't ask to be born and there was a time in my life (when I was very young), when I felt wronged by the universe for being made to exist. There was something upsetting about the realization that I couldn't just choose not to exist without having to do something like destroying this body, which couldn't be achieved without some level of psychological distress at the mere thought of it and in most cases, physical pain too.
Wanting to not exist without having to go through death is one of the most frustrating things to experience.

Anyway,

If we're going to ban consciousness, then let's start with ourselves.

caveats.title: Jev reads intensity, not direction
caveats.text: Emphatic posts on either side get pulled toward Serious: 8 of 18 hand-Reject posts came out Serious in the three-way run, and named rejecters (sapinker, Hesamation, anilkseth) were labelled Serious.

caveats.title: Both camps use the same charged words
caveats.text: "Psychosis", "welfare", "conscious" and "moral patient" appear in rejections and in defences alike, so vocabulary-driven methods (embeddings, and partly Jev) conflate the two. The two-question version still read aleksil79's inversion as dismissive because of its "psychosis" wording.

caveats.title: Small, single-labeller ground truth
caveats.text: 40 random posts plus 67 authors, hand-labelled by one person; ±15 pp at n=40.

caveats.title: Biased sample
caveats.text: 332 posts from relevancy search and flashpoint threads, not a random draw from X. Round 2 is dominated by one news event.

caveats.title: Round 2 has no hand labels
caveats.text: Accuracy figures come from the 40 round-1 hand labels. Round-2 labels are model outputs only, and the three-way question wording for round 2 was rewritten because the round-1 wording was not recorded.

caveats.title: Counts are method-dependent
caveats.text: All-post stance counts swing widely by method (Reject 23%–35%, Serious 28%–48% across the Jev runs). Treat them as method outputs, not population estimates.

caveats.title: Classification is done offline
caveats.text: The agent that renders this page does not classify anything. Labels are produced on the analysis box and committed to the repo.
